scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance emerged in the United States during the 1950s within the rhythm and blues community.
It was initially a novelty step used to vary the movement of the Twist.
It gained significant commercial traction in 1970 following the release of the song 'Do the Funky Chicken' by Rufus Thomas.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Chicken is a secular social dance intended for entertainment and rhythmic expression.
It serves as a lighthearted 'novelty' dance, often used to engage a crowd or provide a rhythmic break in a longer dance set.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: 2019 Father Daughter Dance Promo (https://archive.org/details/2019_Father_Daughter_Dance_Promo)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform lateral body movements while flapping their arms to imitate a chicken's wings.
Simultaneously, the feet are kicked back in a rhythmic fashion.
It was traditionally used as a change-of-pace step during other dances like the Twist.
Watch for The Wing Flap, The Scratch Kick.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (cA28eZCA69Q)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Usually performed in place (stationary) or with minor lateral travel; solo social dance.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is primarily performed to rhythm and blues and funk music.
Key instruments include the electric guitar, bass, drums, and brass sections typical of the Stax Records sound.
Listen for the Electric guitar, Electric bass, Drums, Saxophone.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 110 beats a minute.
A driving funk or R&B sound characterized by a prominent brass section, a syncopated 'popping' bass line, and a steady drum beat that encourages repetitive, rhythmic movement.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: There is no specific traditional costume, as it is a social novelty dance.
It was typically performed in dance halls, clubs, and on televised music programs like Soul Train during its 1970s peak.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Rufus Thomas is the most significant figure associated with the dance's 1970s revival.
Bob Fosse is noted for incorporating elements of the Chicken into the Frug.
While originating in the US R&B scene, the 'Funky Chicken' variant of 1970 is the most distinct evolution, adding funk-era syncopation to the original 1950s R&B step.
The Chicken is a subclass of novelty dance.

scenes.title: Welcome
narration: Chapter 1 — First steps. Today: Master the arm flapping rhythm.
Level: The Basic Wing. Difficulty of the dance overall: beginner.
Your instructor: A high-energy R&B historian who emphasizes the 'groove' over technical perfection.
on_screen: Instructor front view, name of the chapter, the three things you will learn

scenes.title: Body and posture
narration: Slightly crouched or forward-leaning torso to facilitate the bird-like aesthetic.
Arms are bent at the elbows and flapped up and down at the sides like wings.
Lateral (side-to-side) body movements are integrated with the arm and leg motions.
on_screen: Instructor front then side view; freeze-frame on validated posture

scenes.title: Count and rhythm
narration: Count: 1-and-2 / 3-and-4 / 5-and-6 / 7-and-8. The meter is 4/4.
Rhythm pattern: Strong backbeat on 2 and 4 with syncopated bass lines.
Clap it first, then step it in place.
on_screen: Counts on screen, flashing on the beat
Metronome at 77 bpm
scenes.music: lesson_slow (clicks only until the step lands)

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Step 2: Flap both arms at the elbows in imitation of wings
Footwork from the sources: Rhythmic backward kicks of the feet, alternating left and right, often described as 'kicking back their feet'.
Drill: Isolate elbows and flap in 4/4 time
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); repetitions per step: about 4
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Kick one foot back toward the glutes
Step 4: Alternate feet while maintaining lateral body movement
Drill: Add a slight torso lean
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Match the flap to the snare hit
on_screen: Split screen: front view / back view
Tempo label changes: slow → half → full

scenes.title: Common mistakes and what to avoid
narration: Avoid overly stiff posture; the movement should be fluid and lateral rather than strictly vertical.
